messages:
maya: Heads-up — I'm seeing a throughput regression on the FP8 rollout branch when the continuous-batcher sees lots of shape churn. Numbers: p50 token latency +18%, tokens/sec -12% for small-ish 8-64 seq mixes. Not sure if this is a kernel selector thrash or a KV cache side-effect.

oliver: Can you paste the perf profile? is it CPU-bound on the dispatch, or GPU kernel launch overheads?

maya: quick flame (local):
```
%self  cumulative  name
22.4   22.4        kernel_selector::select_best_kernel()
14.1   36.5        continuous_batcher::assemble_batch()
10.8   47.3        kv_cache::merge_prefixes()
8.2    55.5        cuda_launch_overhead
```

maya: so a lot in selector + batcher. selector seems to re-evaluate kernels per-batch more often than before.

sasha: does selector consult calibration metadata per-call? last FP8 patch moved calibration thresholds to be query-time instead of model-load-time to support dynamic quant profiles. could be recomputing expensive heuristics.

maya: yes that's the change. we store raw calib stats and compute quantization plan inline: `plan = make_plan(calib, seq_shape, batch_shape, quant_tolerance)` — that function does a shape normalization pass.

oliver: maybe cache the plan keyed by (model, seq, batch_mode, quant_profile). key size is small. but watch eviction if shapes are high-cardinality.

li: quick note: kv cache hit patterns also change workload shape — when the cache warmup pattern is bursty, continuous batcher pads/repacks differently which nudges kernel selection. Could be a combinatorial effect.

benchbot: Automated microbench run attached (1955003521):
```
workload: 50% seq=16,30% seq=64,20% seq=8
baseline (no FP8 runtime compute): 120k tok/s
fp8-dynamic-plan (no cache): 106k tok/s
fp8-static-plan (precomputed at model load): 118k tok/s
```

benchbot: profiler top(aggregated): selector.compute_plan 19.7%, continuous_batcher.pack 12.6%, kernel_launch 9.3%

maya: interesting — precomputed plan almost recovers baseline. so computing plan on the hot path is the culprit.

henry: two options: 1) memoize plan with TTL and size cap; 2) move plan compute to a background thread and attach when ready (optimistic fast-path uses fallback kernel).

oliver: I worry about memoizing by full shape because batcher produces many transient shapes due to packing. TTL minimal + LRU might work. Also we can canonicalize shapes: treat sequences <=16 as 16, groups [17-32] -> 32, etc. reduces cardinality.

maya: canonicalization is what I was thinking. Also we can detect 'shape noise' — e.g., if same model+quant_profile has >80% of requests within a bucket for a minute, pin that plan.

sasha: earlier we had kernel constraints: some FP8 kernels only support multiples of 8 for hidden dim; if packing produces unaligned widths we fall back to INT8 kernel which is slower. need to measure how often that happens after packer changes.

maya: small sample of kernel dispatch logs (with counts):
```
FP8_kernel_dispatch: 37%
INT8_fallback_dispatch: 51%
FP8_unaligned_dispatch: 12%
```

li: that 51% INT8 fallback is alarming. why would packer change hidden_dim? packer shouldn't touch model hidden dims. but padding can cause interim buffer shapes that cause selector to choose a different kernel due to launch config mismatch.

oliver: right — kernel selector currently bases choice on (hidden, seq, batch) after padding. If padding pushes seq up across threshold or increases effective tile counts, it will flip kernels. two ideas: prefer kernel stability over micro throughput in selector (penalize kernel switches), or prefer kernels that tolerate a wider range of padded shapes.

maya: updated plan:
- canonicalize seq bucket ranges (8,16,32,64)
- compute plan at model-load for default quant profile
- memoize plan keyed on (model, quant_profile, seq_bucket) with LRU cap 256
- add switch-penalty in selector so we avoid flipping kernels for <5% expected perf delta

henry: add telemetry for 'selector_switches_per_minute' + evictions_count. Also tag requests where plan was computed on-path. we need to quantify user impact.

benchbot: quick A/B run (1955004899): with changes above (local) throughput: 118k tok/s, selector CPU% down 60%, FP8 dispatch 62%, INT8 fallback 34%, unaligned 4%.

maya: great improvement. side-effect: slightly higher p95 for tiny seq=8 due to switch-penalty picking a more robust kernel but overall cost better.

oliver: acceptable trade-off. we should also consider making the plan computation much lighter: e.g., precompute only kernel rankings not full micro-configs. then full config can be lazily filled when kernel is actually launched.

sasha: test matrix to run before PR:
- long tail churn workload (seq mixing random)
- KV-warm vs KV-cold workload to ensure cache merge doesn't amplify shape churn
- GPU mem pressure cases where packing changes more often

maya: I'll push a branch with canonicalization + memoization + telemetry and run the full suite tomorrow. putting a canary on dedicated pool to validate in-prod traffic for 24h.

oliver: thanks. tagging @eng-oncall for canary watch. :eyes:

deploy-bot: Canary deploy scheduled to eng-runtime-dedicated-canary at 1955010000 by maya

maya: cc @sasha @li if you see regression telemetry I'll roll back. otherwise I'll open PR with description and microbench results. :thumbsup:
